segments.text: William gives in to The King in Yellow to have his wish granted.
Will finishes his painting, and his soul is taken to Carcosa.
The oppressive darkness fades, replaced by warm golden sunlight streaming through clean, tall windows.
The heavy, suffocating air of the haunted mansion is completely gone.
The scene shifts to a normal, vibrant Blackwood Manor.
Inside the grand dining hall, the fire crackles cheerfully in the hearth.
William, Nathan, Diana, and their parents are gathered together, smiling and laughing as if the tragedies of the past never happened.
For the first time in years, the house feels alive, warm, and whole, the exact family William had always prayed for.
Slowly, the camera begins to pull back, moving away from the laughing family, drifting out through the dining hall window, and rising higher into the sky.
However, the comforting illusion begins to crack at the edges.
Outside the manor’s courtyard, there is no New England forest—only jagged, impossible spires, black stars hanging in a sickly yellow sky, and the dark, endless waters of Lake Hali.
It is revealed that this peaceful Blackwood Manor is actually located deep within Carcosa.
Everything William sees is nothing more than a gilded cage—an illusion crafted by The King to trap William’s soul in Carcosa forever.
Back in the real world, inside the rotting ritual room of the true mansion, William’s empty body stands motionless before the finished canvas, a blank porcelain mask resting quietly over his face.
While his mind sleeps inside a lie, his real body has now become an empty vessel, an actor belonging solely to The King.
Beyond the walls of the manor, the landscape of Blackwood Hollow begins to twist and shift as Carcosa starts to manifest, slowly merging with the valley.
Dark anomalies grow thicker in the fog, reality bends in unimaginable way, and The King’s influence over the world becomes ever stronger.
